quests.instruction: It grows in a brown pod, has sticky sweet-sour pulp around hard seeds and flavors sauces and drinks. Which fruit?
quests.correctAnswer: Tamarind
options: Date
Tamarind
Banana
quests.hint: Think of a pod you crack open.
quests.explanation: Tamarind fits every clue. Date is sticky but has one stone, and banana has no pod.
quests.funFact: Tamarind pods hang from large trees with feathery leaves.

quests.instruction: It has one pit, is bitter until cured and gives oil when pressed. Which fruit?
quests.correctAnswer: Olive
options: Olive
Plum
Cherries
quests.hint: Check the oil and the bitterness.
quests.explanation: Olive fits every clue. Plums and cherries have pits but are not bitter, and they are not pressed for oil.
quests.funFact: Olive trees have gnarled trunks that can look very old.

quests.instruction: It is orange, has a leafy cap and some kinds are puckery until very soft. Which fruit?
quests.correctAnswer: Persimmon
options: Apple
Persimmon
Banana
quests.hint: Think about a fruit with firm kinds and soft kinds.
quests.explanation: Persimmon fits every clue. Apple has no leafy cap, and banana is not orange or puckery.
quests.funFact: Persimmons hang on bare trees like orange lanterns in the cooler months.

quests.instruction: A grown-up halves a kiwi. What is a neat way to remove the flesh?
quests.correctAnswer: Slide a spoon between the skin and the flesh
options: Shake the halves until the flesh falls out
Bite the fuzzy skin off like an apple
Slide a spoon between the skin and the flesh
quests.hint: Think about a curved tool that follows the skin.
quests.explanation: A spoon follows the curve of the skin and lifts out the flesh in one piece.
quests.funFact: The same spoon trick works on avocado halves.

quests.instruction: What is a tidy way for a grown-up to cut an apple into wedges?
quests.correctAnswer: Cut it in quarters, then trim out each core
options: Cut it in quarters, then trim out each core
Cut it into small cubes, core and all
Bite it into rough pieces over the sink
quests.hint: Think about getting rid of the core first.
quests.explanation: Cutting in quarters makes the core easy to trim from each piece, leaving neat wedges.
quests.funFact: A small apple slicer can cut wedges and remove the core in one push.

quests.instruction: How should berries be stored so they last longer?
quests.correctAnswer: In a single layer in a container with air holes
options: Packed tightly in a sealed jar to keep air out
Piled high in a deep bowl on the counter
In a single layer in a container with air holes
quests.hint: Think about crushing and moisture.
quests.explanation: A single layer with some airflow keeps berries from crushing each other and from getting damp.
quests.funFact: Crushed berries spoil faster and can spread mold to others.

quests.instruction: Why do bananas curve upward as they grow?
quests.correctAnswer: They grow away from the ground, toward the light
options: They bend because heavy bunches weigh them down
They are pushed upward by the soil underneath
They grow away from the ground, toward the light
quests.hint: Think about what a plant grows toward.
quests.explanation: Banana fruits grow away from the ground and toward the light, which curves them upward.
quests.funFact: Bananas on a plant point upward in a bunch.

quests.instruction: Why do many fruits have thick skin or a hard shell?
quests.correctAnswer: To protect the fruit and its seeds
options: To hide the fruit's color from animals
To protect the fruit and its seeds
To make the fruit lighter to carry
quests.hint: Think about what the fruit needs to survive.
quests.explanation: Thick skins and shells protect the soft flesh and the seeds from damage, pests and drying out.
quests.funFact: Coconut shells and pomegranate skins are both strong protectors.

quests.instruction: Why are fruit trees often planted in rows with space between them?
quests.correctAnswer: So each tree gets sunlight and workers can reach the fruit
options: So each tree gets sunlight and workers can reach the fruit
So the trees stay small and the fruit stays sweeter
So the roots can tangle together and share water
quests.hint: Think about light and walking space.
quests.explanation: Rows give each tree room to catch sunlight and let workers and machines move between the trees.
quests.funFact: Space between trees also lets air flow, which helps keep leaves healthy.

quests.instruction: Which usually keeps fresh longer in the fridge?
quests.correctAnswer: Apples
options: Strawberries
Raspberries
Apples
quests.hint: Think about skin and firmness.
quests.explanation: Apples have thick skin and firm flesh, so they last for weeks, while soft berries last only a few days.
quests.funFact: Some apples are kept in cold storage for months before they reach the shops.

quests.instruction: Line up a cherry, an apple, a pineapple and a jackfruit from lightest to heaviest. Which is third?
quests.correctAnswer: Pineapple
options: Pineapple
Apple
Jackfruit
quests.hint: Put them in order from the lightest.
quests.explanation: The order is cherry, apple, pineapple, jackfruit, so the pineapple is third.
quests.funFact: A single jackfruit can weigh more than ten kilograms.

quests.instruction: A whole watermelon costs 6 coins and weighs 6 kg. Pre-cut watermelon costs 2 coins per kg. Which costs less per kg?
quests.correctAnswer: The whole watermelon
options: The pre-cut watermelon
The whole watermelon
They cost the same
quests.hint: Divide the price by the weight.
quests.explanation: The whole watermelon costs 1 coin per kg, while the pre-cut watermelon costs 2 coins per kg.
quests.funFact: Pre-cut fruit costs more because of the extra work.

quests.instruction: You find a new fruit with a thick, spiky husk and a very strong smell. What is the most sensible plan?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask a grown-up to open it and find out how it is eaten
options: Ask a grown-up to open it and find out how it is eaten
Bite hard into the husk to see what is inside
Open it yourself with the sharpest knife you have
quests.hint: Think about safety first.
quests.explanation: A spiky husk is hard and sharp, so a grown-up should open it and help you learn how to eat it.
quests.funFact: Fruits with thick husks are opened carefully, sometimes with special tools.

quests.instruction: A new berry is wrapped in a papery, lantern-shaped husk. How would you eat it?
quests.correctAnswer: Peel back the husk and eat the berry inside
options: Eat the husk first and the berry after
Squeeze it like a lemon to get the juice
Peel back the husk and eat the berry inside
quests.hint: Think about unwrapping.
quests.explanation: The papery husk is not eaten. Peel it back and enjoy the berry inside.
quests.funFact: Many fruits come with their own natural wrapping.

quests.instruction: A new fruit grows on a climbing vine and has a tough rind with juicy, seedy pulp inside. How might you eat it?
quests.correctAnswer: Cut it open and scoop out the pulp
options: Cut it open and scoop out the pulp
Eat the tough rind and leave the pulp
Peel off the rind and cook it first
quests.hint: Think about how you would eat a fruit with a hard rind and soft inside.
quests.explanation: A tough rind protects soft pulp, so you cut the fruit open and scoop out the pulp.
quests.funFact: You can learn how to eat a new fruit by looking at how it is built.

quests.instruction: Which statement about ripening is the most accurate?
quests.correctAnswer: Some fruit keeps ripening after picking and some does not
options: Every fruit keeps on ripening after it is picked
Some fruit keeps ripening after picking and some does not
No fruit ever ripens again once it has been picked
quests.hint: Remember bananas and strawberries.
quests.explanation: Bananas and avocados keep ripening after picking, while strawberries and grapes do not.
quests.funFact: Bananas, avocados and pears are among the fruits that ripen after picking.

quests.instruction: Which is the most accurate way to describe fruit seeds?
quests.correctAnswer: Tiny seeds like kiwi seeds are eaten, but hard pits are set aside
options: All seeds and pits should be swallowed with the fruit
Tiny seeds like kiwi seeds are eaten, but hard pits are set aside
Only seeds from tropical fruits can ever be eaten
quests.hint: Think about kiwi and cherries.
quests.explanation: Tiny seeds like those in kiwi are eaten, while hard pits and big stones are set aside.
quests.funFact: Even some large seeds, like pumpkin seeds, are roasted and eaten.

quests.instruction: What is the most accurate thing to say about fruit peels?
quests.correctAnswer: Whether to eat the peel depends on the fruit
options: Every fruit peel should be eaten to avoid waste
Peels should only be eaten after being cooked
Whether to eat the peel depends on the fruit
quests.hint: Think about apples and oranges.
quests.explanation: Apple skin is eaten but orange peel is not, so it depends on the fruit.
quests.funFact: Some peels, like orange zest, are used in small amounts to add flavor.

quests.instruction: Which five-day snack plan has the most variety and travels well?
quests.correctAnswer: Apple, mandarin, grapes, banana, pear
options: Banana every day
Cut melon, raspberries, sliced peaches, cut mango, strawberries
Apple, mandarin, grapes, banana, pear
quests.hint: Think about different kinds and sturdy fruit.
quests.explanation: The first plan offers five different fruits that all travel well without a fridge.
quests.funFact: Planning snacks ahead makes it easier to eat a variety of fruits.

quests.instruction: A smoothie for 4 people uses 2 bananas. How many bananas are needed for 8 people?
quests.hint: Twice as many people needs twice as much.
quests.explanation: 8 people is double 4 people, so double the 2 bananas to get 4 bananas.
quests.funFact: Scaling a recipe means changing every ingredient by the same amount.

quests.instruction: You have 15 coins. Grapes cost 6 coins and apples cost 3 coins each. After buying the grapes, how many apples can you buy?
quests.hint: Subtract the grapes, then divide by 3.
quests.explanation: 15 minus 6 leaves 9, and 9 divided by 3 is 3 apples.
quests.funFact: Budgeting means planning what to buy with the money you have.

quests.instruction: You test lemon juice on one apple slice and nothing on another. After 30 minutes, what do you expect?
quests.correctAnswer: The slice with lemon juice will brown less
options: The slice with lemon juice will brown less
The slice with lemon juice will brown faster
Both slices will brown at exactly the same rate
quests.hint: Remember what the acid does.
quests.explanation: Lemon juice slows the browning reaction, so the treated slice should look fresher.
quests.funFact: Scientists make a prediction like this before they test, and call it a hypothesis.

quests.instruction: What is a good way to record the results of a fruit experiment?
quests.correctAnswer: Take photos or write notes at set times
options: Remember it all without writing anything
Take photos or write notes at set times
Guess the results at the very end
quests.hint: Think about how to compare changes over time.
quests.explanation: Photos or notes taken at set times let you compare what changed.
quests.funFact: Measuring at the same times each day keeps the test fair.

quests.instruction: Your fruit experiment gives a surprising result. What should a scientist do?
quests.correctAnswer: Repeat the test and check what changed
options: Ignore the result
Repeat the test and check what changed
Change the numbers to match the guess
quests.hint: Surprises are a chance to learn.
quests.explanation: Repeating the test and checking for differences shows whether the surprising result is reliable.
quests.funFact: Many scientific discoveries began with a surprise.

quests.instruction: How can you politely refuse a fruit you cannot eat because of an allergy?
quests.correctAnswer: Say, "No thank you, I have an allergy"
options: Say, "No thank you, I have an allergy"
Eat it anyway so nobody feels bad
Say nothing and quietly hide it away
quests.hint: Think about staying safe and being kind.
quests.explanation: A short, polite explanation keeps you safe and shows others how to help.
quests.funFact: Telling people about your allergy helps them cook safely for you.

quests.instruction: A friend asks what is in the fruit salad you made. What is the best answer?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell them all the ingredients honestly
options: Say it is only apples to keep it simple
Say you do not remember what is in it
Tell them all the ingredients honestly
quests.hint: Think about allergies and trust.
quests.explanation: Listing every ingredient helps people avoid foods they cannot eat.
quests.funFact: Cooks at restaurants also share ingredient lists on request.

quests.instruction: A dried fruit mix says "may contain traces of nuts." Who should be careful with it?
quests.correctAnswer: People with nut allergies
options: Only people over 100
People with nut allergies
Nobody needs to read it
quests.hint: Think about why the warning is there.
quests.explanation: The warning tells people with nut allergies that the mix may have come into contact with nuts.
quests.funFact: Reading labels is a helpful habit for everyone.

quests.instruction: Which shows you understand fruit best?
quests.correctAnswer: Explaining how it grows, how to pick it and handle it
options: Knowing its name in as many languages as possible
Remembering how many fruits fit in a big box
Explaining how it grows, how to pick it and handle it
quests.hint: Think about everything you have learned.
quests.explanation: Knowing where fruit comes from, how to choose it and how to prepare it safely shows real understanding.
quests.funFact: You started this journey by learning a few fruit names, and now you know how fruit grows, ripens and is eaten.

quests.instruction: Which list puts the journey of a fruit in the right order?
quests.correctAnswer: Flower, pollination, growing fruit, ripening, picking, shop
options: Flower, pollination, growing fruit, ripening, picking, shop
Seed, picking, pollination, flower, shop, ripening
Shop, ripening, flower, growing fruit, picking, pollination
quests.hint: Start where a fruit begins and end where you buy it.
quests.explanation: A fruit starts as a flower, is pollinated, grows, ripens, is picked and then reaches the shop.
quests.funFact: Along the way, bees, sunshine, water and farmers all play a part.

quests.instruction: It grows in hands on a tall plant, is picked green, ripens to yellow and is peeled by hand. Which fruit?
quests.correctAnswer: Banana
options: Banana
Mango
Papaya
quests.hint: This was the first fruit you met in this game.
quests.explanation: Banana fits every clue. Mango and papaya do not grow in hands and are not peeled the same way.
quests.funFact: A banana plant can give its first bunch within about a year of planting.
